subject: Clarify SOC 2 point-in-time snapshot: inclusivity and UTC cutoff
message_1_subject: Question on SOC 2 report date / snapshot inclusivity
message_1_body:
Hi Olga,

We're preparing to complete our control testing and need to confirm the exact coverage semantics of the SOC 2 Type II report you provided. The PDF lists an audit period that ends on 2026-06-30. For our testing we need two clarifications: 1) Does the point-in-time snapshot for 2026-06-30 include all events up to 23:59:59 UTC on that date (i.e., inclusive)? 2) For month-based evidence (logs, config snapshots) do you provide an end-of-day export or a system snapshot at a particular UTC timestamp?

We may need short-lived evidence extracts for specific hours on 2026-06-30. Can you also confirm whether you can produce a bridge letter if there is any known gap between the audit period and a recent configuration change?

Attaching your SOC 2 report we pulled from your portal. Appreciate a quick confirmation — our control window closes next Friday.

Thanks,
Sarah Lam
Senior IT Auditor
Acme Corp

Attachments: SOC2_TypeII_2026-06-30.pdf (we attached your copy)
message_2_subject: Re: Question on SOC 2 report date / snapshot inclusivity
message_2_body:
Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the clear questions. Short answers first: 1) The SOC 2 Type II period reported (ending 2026-06-30) is inclusive through 23:59:59 UTC on 2026-06-30 for system-level artifacts we export as point-in-time snapshots. 2) For monthly evidence we typically produce an end-of-day export extracted at 23:59:00 UTC.

A couple of important implementation notes:
- For logs stored in our ingestion system, exports are truncated to the last processed offset at 23:59:59 UTC; there can be a small ingest latency for a handful of milliseconds but we treat the snapshot as inclusive.
- For configuration snapshots (compute, infra-as-code state), our export captures the configuration reported by the control plane at the stated UTC timestamp.

If you need extracts for narrower hourly windows on 2026-06-30 we can run ad-hoc exports, but those need to be requested and scheduled so we can pin the exact export timestamp and hash the result.

On bridge letters: we can provide a bridge letter for any changes that occur after the report cutoff; those are issued by Product Security and reference the date range and the controls unaffected by the change. If you expect to need one, please confirm the scope and whether it should be signed by our CISO or VP Security.

I've cc'ed Karthik for contract/Procurement visibility and Vivek to coordinate timing with your audit team.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: SOC2_TypeII_2026-06-30.pdf (we have your copy here).

message_4_subject: Re: Question on SOC 2 report date / snapshot inclusivity — bridge letter and timing
message_4_body:
Hi Sarah —

Thanks for looping us in. We can prepare a bridge letter if Acme requires it; typical contents are: scope of the original report, statement of no control exceptions identified since cutoff (or list of changes if applicable), and the exact bridge coverage dates. Turnaround is ordinarily 4 business days from receipt of the exact scope and any change-ticket references. If the request is urgent we can expedite to 2 business days with approval from security leadership.

What we need from you to proceed:
1) Confirm the artifacts you want (logs, config snapshots, user-provisioning audit).
2) Confirm the hourly slices (you mentioned 15:00 UTC on 2026-06-30) and any additional timestamps.
3) State whether Acme requires the bridge letter to be signed by our CISO (Anika Rao) or by the VP, Trust (Olga).

Once you confirm items 1–3 we'll kick off the evidence export and the bridge-letter draft. I've attached our standard bridge-letter template so you can preview the language.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
